paper.title: A novel model to combine clinical and pathway-based transcriptomic information for the prognosis prediction of breast cancer
paper.citation: Huang S, Yee C, Ching T, Yu H, Garmire LX. A novel model to combine clinical and pathway-based transcriptomic information for the prognosis prediction of breast cancer. PLoS Comput Biol 10(9):e1003851 (2014)

missing_time.what: Two Miller patients have a relapse status (one relapse, one censored) but no relapse time in breastCancerUPP; their time is 0
missing_time.sensitivity: With time 0 the five Fig. 1 log-rank p-values for p53, grade, LN, ER and PG, all four univariate Cox p-values of Table 2 and Table 1's mean RFS (8.168, printed 8.167) come back; dropping the two patients gives none of them (LN 1.10e-7 against 4.93e-8, grade 0.00156 against 0.00181, mean RFS 8.237).

p53_missing.what: Four Miller tumours without p53 sequencing status count as wild type
p53_missing.sensitivity: Table 1 prints 55 mutated, 181 wild type and 0 unknown for Miller, and GSE4922 has 55 mutated, 177 wild type and 4 unknown for these tumours. Dropping them gives the Fig. 1A chi-square p 0.0696 instead of 0.088.

miller_clinical.what: Miller's relapse-free survival, ER, PgR, size, grade, node and age from Bioconductor breastCancerUPP 1.40.0; p53 status from the GSE4922 clinical file (same Uppsala tumours)
miller_clinical.sensitivity: GEO GSE3494 has no clinical data. The 236 tumours with a relapse status in breastCancerUPP give Table 1's counts (55 relapses, ER 201/31/4, grade 62/121/51/2, LN 78/149/9, mean age 62.51); GSE4922's disease-free survival for the same tumours gives other log-rank p-values (LN 2.5e-4 against 4.93e-8).

pawitan_time.what: Pawitan's relapse-free time is the earlier of SURV_RELAPSE and SURV_DEATH (GSE1456); the event is RELAPSE
pawitan_time.sensitivity: Its mean, 5.959 years, is Table 1's; SURV_RELAPSE alone gives 6.196.

gene_sets.what: The 403 gene sets are MSigDB v6.0 c2.cp.biocarta (217) and c2.cp.kegg (186), as gene symbols
gene_sets.sensitivity: The release the paper used (2013 or 2014, MSigDB 3.x or 4.0) is not on the public download server. v6.0 has the 403 sets and all 15 of Table 2, and gives Table 3's genomic counts and weights exactly; v6.2 is identical.

probes.what: Probes are mapped to gene symbols with GEO's current GPL96 annotation; probes for several genes are left out; a gene's value is the geometric mean of its probes' log2 values
probes.sensitivity: The paper mapped through RefSeq with biomaRt (release not given). 12,502 genes; the paper's 'over 14,000' is not reached by any count we tried (13,909 with multi-gene probes).

normalization.what: Each data set is quantile normalized on its own (limma normalizeBetweenArrays); no CONOR batch correction
normalization.sensitivity: The paper does not name the limma method. pathifier standardizes every gene within each data set before scoring, which removes any per-gene location and scale shift such as CONOR's empirical Bayes (ComBat) correction; it is left out for that reason.

pathifier.what: pathifier 1.40.0 with its defaults (attempts 100, min_exp 4, min_std 0.4, maximize_stability), no normal samples (none of the data sets has any), one set of subsamplings (seed 1) per data set, each data set scored on its own; each score is turned, if needed, so that it rises with the mean standardized expression of its pathway's genes
pathifier.sensitivity: Without normal samples pathifier's curve starts from the first principal component and which end scores 0 is arbitrary; the paper does not say how it handled this. The orientation rule decides the sign of every coefficient and whether a training-set model carries to a test set.

lasso.what: Penalty: the median of the optimal lambda1 of 250 runs of penalized::optL1 with 10 random folds each (seed 1); PDS not standardized for the genomic model; clinical and combined inputs standardized to mean 0 and SD 1 within each data set; missing clinical values filled with the median
lasso.sensitivity: The paper gives no folds, grid, seed or rule for turning 250 runs into one lambda. On the clinical model the 250 runs' optimal lambda ranges over a factor of about 2, which moves the coefficients but not the selected features.

cutoff.what: Higher risk: prognostic index above the training set's 3rd quartile (Figs 4 and 6); above the quantile at the set's relapse share for Fig. 5 and the leave-one-out runs

logrank.what: The 'Wilcoxon log-rank test' is survival::survdiff with rho = 0 (the log-rank test)
logrank.sensitivity: rho = 0 gives the five Fig. 1 p-values as printed; rho = 1 (Peto-Wilcoxon) gives none (LN 1.56e-8 against 4.93e-8).

p_scale.what: Model-dependent p-values are compared as -log10(p) within 1 (the same order of magnitude) and AUCs within 0.03
p_scale.sensitivity: The models depend on random cross-validation folds and unstated settings, so no run can be expected to print the paper's digits; values that depend only on the data are compared at printed precision.

items.label: Fig. 5 and text, log-rank p and AUC of the gene- and pathway-based models

cause.summary: The pathway models are fitted on our pathway scores, which are not the paper's (table2.genomic_univariate); the gene models on our gene-level expression, whose mapping and normalization may differ from the paper's (biomaRt through RefSeq, CONOR), so Pawitan's and Ivshina's gene models differ too. Desmedt has almost no relapse signal in our hands: no pathway has univariate p below 0.008 and no gene below 3.4e-5 (of 7,455 expressed), so cross-validation picks a penalty (pathways 4.7 to 6.2, genes 47 to 79) that keeps nothing and both Desmedt models are empty. The paper's Desmedt pathway result (p 5.12e-36, AUC 0.92 on 198 patients) is close to what a penalty near 1 gives in-sample: 77 pathways, p 2.8e-37, AUC 0.94.

page.items_caption: Every figure panel, table and number of the paper, with our value and the verdict computed from results.json.
page.claims_line: The paper's main claim does not hold on our run: the pathway model is weaker than printed and does not carry to Desmedt. Adding clinical features does help it on both sets (AUC 0.81 against 0.73 on Miller, 0.69 against 0.67 on Ivshina). Ivshina is not an independent test set: 232 of its 249 arrays are Miller's.
came_back: pathifier scores, the penalized Cox model with 250 cross-validations, the prognostic index and its cutoffs, the clinical, combined, gene-based and NKI70 models, as the R package pdscox.

Table 1's counts for all four data sets, once Miller's clinical data were found in breastCancerUPP (GEO has none); left over are a swapped PgR row and rounding in the paper, the size-class boundaries, and one Ivshina tumour under 10 mm (15 against 14).

11 of its 12 printed p-values (the chi-square and log-rank tests of the clinical factors; not the PAM50 clusters), and the four Kaplan-Meier panels within 2 px (96 to 98% of the published curve pixels).
The same four features (lymph node, size, grade, p53) with coefficients within 0.05 of Table 2, and the four univariate p-values as printed.
The genomic model's top 30 genes with their counts and weights, 60 of 60 fields, from the paper's own pathways and hazard ratios.
Its log-rank p and AUC on the training set, as printed in Fig. S3.
buried: The paper's pathway scores: on ours, 11 of its 15 selected pathways have univariate p-values more than ten times larger (VIP, LYSOSOME, AKAP13 and LINOLEIC ACID at p 0.5 to 0.8 instead of 2e-6 to 4e-3). On five of them, other seeds, no normalization, no gene filters, no stability option or linear input did not bring them back.
So our genomic model keeps 5 pathways (3 of the paper's) instead of 15, and the test sets come out weaker than printed: Desmedt p 0.69 against 3.73e-4.
Desmedt's own models: cross-validation keeps no gene and no pathway; the paper's p 5.12e-36 and AUC 0.92 need a penalty far below the cross-validated one.
The PAM50 clusters of Fig. 1A and the pathway clusters of Fig. 3: no clustering we tried reaches the printed p-values (best 0.011 against 7.46e-5, and 7.4e-4 against 1.99e-6).
Fig. S1: with fewer pathways the AUC hardly falls (median 0.715 to 0.707).
matched: Typed from the paper; counts as printed, percentages within one point, model p-values within one order of magnitude, AUCs within 0.03.
Our curves drawn on each published panel's pixel grid, placed through its tick marks and scored within 2 px against controls (shifted and swapped curves).
Each written as a comparison; the 9 that rest on the paper's own numbers hold there.
page.closing: We dug up Huang et al. 2014 on 18 Nov 2026.

status_note: the pathway Cox-LASSO pipeline rebuilt as the R package `pdscox`; Table 1, Fig. 1's 11 p-values and Kaplan-Meier curves, the clinical model, Table 3's genomic genes and NKI70 come back; our pathway scores of the paper's 15 pathways are weaker, so the genomic model keeps 5, Desmedt is not predicted (p 0.69 against 3.73e-4) and the pathway-over-gene claims do not hold; Ivshina shares 232 of 249 arrays with the training set
site_note: Clinical results come back; the pathway model does not
